THE PROCESS

Seven steps from blank wall to finished mural

You approve each one before we move on. No paint until the sketch is right.

A1
C3
D4
A1

Measure & sketch

We measure the wall, talk it through and hand you a scaled color sketch to approve.

B2

Scale & transfer

The sketch gets gridded at full size so every line lands where it should.

C3

Chalk the grid

Faint chalk lines on your wall show exactly where every shape begins.

D4

Block in color

Flat color goes down first so you can see the composition at full scale.

E5

Detail & shade

Brushwork, shadows and highlights bring the scene to life.

F6

Clear coat

A UV-resistant top coat seals exterior walls against sun and rain.

G7

Walk-through

We walk the wall with you and touch up anything that isn't right.

WHAT WE PAINT

Walls, doors, fences and windows

Every surface gets its own prep plan and finish.

D4 · SAMPLE REVIEWS

What homeowners say after the wall is done

4.9 out of 5 · 86 reviews (Sample) Sample review

  • "Ximena brought the sketch on paper, then chalked a grid right on our stucco wall so we could see where every leaf would go. Our backyard wall in Highland Park went from beige to bougainvillea in four days."
    — Teodora M., Los Angeles · Exterior murals
  • "We were five weeks from the due date and nervous. They gave us a schedule backwards from it, painted a fox and a hill under a night sky, and aired the room out a week early."
    — Kwabena O., Glendale · Nursery and kids' room murals
  • "Our bakery window lettering is all hand brushed now. Clean edges, a little gold shadow, done before we opened at seven."
    — Lourdes F., Pasadena · Hand-lettered signs
  • "The garage door got tagged three times last year. Since the mural went up with the clear coat, one tag showed up and wiped right off with their kit. Neighbors stop to look now."
    — Benedikt A., Burbank · Garage door and fence art
  • "They painted the dining room wall from six to ten each morning so we never closed. The fans were off by lunch and the paint smell was gone by dinner."
    — Yesenia C., Alhambra · Restaurant and cafe walls
  • "I was sure I wanted a big landscape. The scale sketch showed it would swallow our stairwell, so we went smaller and much better. Paying for the sketch first was worth it."
    — Harlan P., South Pasadena · Design sketch and consult
